stem: Which metal is the **most** reactive?

options.rationale: Copper is near the bottom of the series.
Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series.
Zinc is in the middle of the series.
Magnesium is below potassium, sodium and calcium.

explanation: The order is K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, (C), Zn, Fe, (H), Cu, Ag, Au. Potassium is the most reactive of these.

stem: Which pair of metals **both** react with dilute hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen?

options.rationale: Zinc reacts, but copper is below hydrogen and does not.
Both are above hydrogen in the reactivity series.
Iron reacts slowly, but gold is below hydrogen and does not react.
Magnesium reacts, but silver is below hydrogen and does not.

explanation: Only metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series, such as magnesium, zinc and iron, react with dilute acids to give hydrogen. Copper, silver and gold are below hydrogen and do not react.

stem: True or false: zinc displaces magnesium from magnesium sulfate solution.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not quite: zinc is less reactive than magnesium, so it cannot displace it. No reaction occurs.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct: zinc is below magnesium in the reactivity series, so there is no reaction.

explanation:
A metal can only displace a less reactive metal from a solution of its ions. Magnesium is more reactive than zinc, so zinc has no effect on magnesium sulfate solution.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*

stem: Which mixture would react?

options.rationale: Silver is less reactive than copper.
Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper.
Iron is less reactive than magnesium.
Copper is less reactive than zinc, so no displacement occurs.

explanation:
$\ce{Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu}$: the more reactive metal (zinc) displaces the less reactive metal (copper) from its solution.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*

stem: Where is **carbon** placed in the reactivity series?

options.rationale: Metals below carbon can be extracted by heating their oxides with carbon.
That is the position of hydrogen.
Carbon is not more reactive than potassium.
Carbon can reduce many metal oxides, so it is well above gold.

explanation: The order is K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, C, Zn, Fe, H, Cu, Ag, Au. Carbon sits between aluminium and zinc.

stem: Which metal reacts only extremely slowly with cold water but reacts rapidly when heated in **steam**?

options.rationale: Sodium reacts vigorously with cold water.
Heated magnesium burns brightly in steam, forming magnesium oxide and hydrogen.
Gold does not react with water or steam.
Copper does not react with water or steam.

explanation: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water but rapidly with steam: $\ce{Mg + H2O -> MgO + H2}$.

stem: Zinc powder is stirred into blue copper(II) sulfate solution. What would be observed?

options.content: The solution turns darker blue and the zinc grows larger.
options.rationale: Copper(II) ions are used up, so the blue colour fades.

options.content: The blue colour fades, a red-brown solid forms and the mixture gets warm.
options.rationale: Copper is displaced and copper(II) ions are removed from the solution.

options.content: Bubbles of hydrogen form and the solution stays blue.
options.rationale: No gas is produced in a displacement reaction.

options.content: There is no visible change, because zinc is less reactive than copper is.
options.rationale: Zinc is more reactive than copper.

explanation:
Zinc displaces copper: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Red-brown copper forms, the blue colour fades as Cu²⁺ ions are removed (zinc sulfate is colourless), and the reaction is exothermic.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*
hints: Which ion makes copper(II) sulfate solution blue?

stem: Which ionic equation represents the reaction of zinc with copper(II) sulfate solution?

options.rationale: Zinc atoms lose electrons; copper(II) ions gain them.
Sulfate ions are spectator ions.
Charges are not balanced: zinc must become Zn²⁺.
This is the reverse reaction, which does not happen.

explanation:
The sulfate ions are spectators. Zinc atoms form ions and copper ions form atoms: $\ce{Zn + Cu^2+ -> Zn^2+ + Cu}$.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*

stem:
Metals P, Q and R are each added to solutions of the nitrates of the other two metals. ✓ = a reaction is seen; ✗ = no reaction.

| Metal | P nitrate | Q nitrate | R nitrate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | – | ✗ | ✓ |
| Q | ✓ | – | ✓ |
| R | ✗ | ✗ | – |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?

options.rationale: Q displaces two metals, P displaces one, R displaces none.
This is the reverse order.
Q displaces P, so Q is more reactive than P.
P displaces R, so P is more reactive than R.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The three metals are copper, iron and zinc. Which one is R?

options.rationale: R is the least reactive of the three.
Iron is in the middle, so it would be P.
Zinc is the most reactive of the three, so it would be Q.
The order identifies the least reactive metal.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why there is no reaction when R is added to the nitrate of P.

points.description: R is less reactive than P, so it cannot displace P from its compound / has a lower tendency to form ions

parts.explanation: R is less reactive than P. A metal can only displace a less reactive metal, so R cannot take P's place in the compound.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Which of the three metals would react with dilute hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen?

options.rationale: Iron (P) is also above hydrogen, although it reacts slowly.
R is the least reactive and is below hydrogen.
Copper (R) is below hydrogen and does not react.
Iron and zinc are above hydrogen; copper is below it.

explanation:
Q displaces both other metals (most reactive), P displaces only R, and R displaces neither: Q > P > R, so Q = zinc, P = iron and R = copper. Zinc and iron are above hydrogen and react with dilute acids; copper does not.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*
hints: Count the ticks for each metal.

stem: Aluminium is above zinc in the reactivity series, but an aluminium pan does not react with water. Why?

options.content: Water is not able to react with any metal at all.
options.rationale: Reactive metals such as sodium react violently with water.

options.content: Aluminium is below hydrogen in the reactivity series.
options.rationale: Aluminium is well above hydrogen.

options.content: A thin, tough oxide layer stops water reaching the metal.
options.rationale: The oxide layer protects the aluminium.

options.content: Aluminium is really less reactive than zinc.
options.rationale: Aluminium is more reactive than zinc.

explanation:
Aluminium is covered by a protective layer of aluminium oxide that forms as soon as the metal meets air, so aluminium appears much less reactive than its position suggests.

*Syllabus note: Cambridge IGCSE Supplement (Extended) content.*
hints: What forms on the surface of aluminium in air?

stem: Equal-sized pieces of four metals are placed in dilute hydrochloric acid. Metal W fizzes vigorously, X fizzes slowly, Y shows no change and Z fizzes steadily. What is the order of reactivity, most reactive first?

options.rationale: Steady fizzing (Z) shows a faster reaction than slow fizzing (X).
This is the reverse order.
Vigorous fizzing (W) is faster than steady fizzing (Z).
Vigorous > steady > slow > none.

explanation: The faster the metal reacts with the acid, the more reactive it is: W (vigorous) > Z (steady) > X (slow) > Y (no reaction).

stem: $1.30\ \text{g}$ of zinc powder is added to excess copper(II) sulfate solution. Calculate the maximum mass of copper that can be displaced. $\ce{Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu}$ (Ar: Cu = 64, Zn = 65)
explanation:
$n(\ce{Zn}) = 1.30 \div 65 = 0.0200$ mol, so $0.0200$ mol of copper forms: $0.0200 \times 64 = 1.28\ \text{g}$.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*

stem: Equal masses of four metal powders are added, in turn, to 25 cm³ portions of the same copper(II) sulfate solution. The temperature rises are: magnesium 14.5 °C, zinc 7.0 °C, iron 3.5 °C and silver 0.0 °C. Which conclusion is correct?

options.content: Silver is the most reactive, because it reacted so fast that its temperature did not change.
options.rationale: No temperature change means no reaction.

options.content: Iron is more reactive than zinc.
options.rationale: Iron gave a smaller temperature rise than zinc.

options.content: The order of reactivity is Mg > Zn > Fe > Ag, and silver does not displace copper.
options.rationale: A larger temperature rise shows a more vigorous displacement reaction.
Silver gave no temperature rise: it is below copper and does not react.

explanation:
Displacement reactions are exothermic. The further a metal is above copper, the more energy is released and the larger the temperature rise. Silver is below copper, so there is no reaction.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*
hints: What does a larger temperature rise tell you about the reaction?

The blue solution becomes paler (fades) / turns pale green

Water does not take part.

Copper(II) ions gain electrons.

stem: Metal M reacts slowly with dilute hydrochloric acid. It displaces copper from copper(II) sulfate solution but does **not** displace zinc from zinc sulfate solution. Where does M belong in the reactivity series?

options.content: between hydrogen and copper, below zinc
options.rationale: It reacts with dilute acid, so it is above hydrogen.
It displaces copper, so it is above copper.
It cannot displace zinc, so it is below zinc.

options.content: between zinc and copper, above hydrogen
options.rationale: It is less reactive than zinc but more reactive than copper, and it reacts with acid.

explanation:
Displacing copper puts M above copper; failing to displace zinc puts it below zinc; reacting with dilute acid puts it above hydrogen. M behaves like iron.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*

stem: Plan an experiment using displacement reactions to put magnesium, zinc and copper in order of reactivity. You are given pieces of each metal and solutions of magnesium sulfate, zinc sulfate and copper(II) sulfate. [5]

points.description: Put a piece of each metal into a sample of each of the other two metals' sulfate solutions (e.g. in a spotting tile or test tubes)
Use the same volume and concentration of solution and similar-sized pieces of metal
Look for a coating forming on the metal / a colour change in the solution (or measure the temperature rise)
Record the results in a table (reaction / no reaction)
The metal that displaces both others is the most reactive; the one that displaces neither is the least reactive

answerSpec.modelAnswer: Clean the metals with sandpaper. Put the same volume of each sulfate solution into separate test tubes and add a similar-sized piece of each metal to the solutions of the other two metals (six tests in all). Watch for a coating forming on the metal or a change in the colour of the solution, which shows a reaction; a thermometer could also record any temperature rise. Record ✓ or ✗ in a table. The metal that displaces both of the others is the most reactive (magnesium), the metal that displaces one is in the middle (zinc), and the metal that displaces neither is the least reactive (copper).

explanation:
A fair plan tests every metal with the other metals' solutions, controls the variables, states what counts as a reaction and explains how the results give the order.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*
hints: How many metal–solution combinations are needed?

rejected.feedback: Hydrogen is also between zinc and copper, but it is not a metal.
Tin is not in the series used in this course.
Lead is not in the series used in this course.

explanation: The order is …, zinc, iron, (hydrogen), copper, … Iron is the only metal in the list between zinc and copper.

stem: Simple cells are made by placing two different metals in salt solution. Which pair of metals would give the **largest** voltage?

options.rationale: Zinc and iron are close together in the series.
Zinc is below magnesium, so this pair is closer together.
These metals are furthest apart in the reactivity series.
Iron and copper are closer together than magnesium and copper.

explanation:
The further apart two metals are in the reactivity series, the larger the voltage of the cell. The more reactive metal (here magnesium) is the negative electrode.

*Syllabus note: using the reactivity series to explain cells is ZIMSEC O-Level content.*
hints: Find the pair that is furthest apart in the series.

stem: Excess magnesium powder is stirred into a solution containing both copper(II) ions and zinc ions until no further change occurs. The mixture is then filtered. What is in the residue and in the filtrate?

options.content: residue: magnesium only; filtrate: copper(II) ions and zinc ions
options.rationale: Magnesium is more reactive than both, so they are displaced.

options.content: residue: copper only; filtrate: zinc ions and magnesium ions
options.rationale: With magnesium in excess, the zinc is displaced as well.

options.content: residue: zinc only; filtrate: copper(II) ions and magnesium ions
options.rationale: Copper is the least reactive, so it is displaced first.

options.content: residue: copper, zinc and unreacted magnesium; filtrate: magnesium ions
options.rationale: Magnesium is above both copper and zinc, so it displaces both; the excess remains.

explanation:
Magnesium is more reactive than both zinc and copper, so excess magnesium displaces both metals from solution. The residue is copper, zinc and leftover magnesium; only magnesium ions (with the original anions) remain in solution.

*Syllabus note: displacement reactions with metal ions are Cambridge IGCSE Supplement content and are in the ZIMSEC O-Level syllabus.*
hints: Compare magnesium with each of the two metals in solution.

stem: True or false: iron reacts more vigorously with dilute hydrochloric acid than magnesium does.

answerSpec.feedbackTrue: Not quite: magnesium is more reactive than iron, so it fizzes much faster.
answerSpec.feedbackFalse: Correct: magnesium is higher in the reactivity series, so it reacts more vigorously than iron.

explanation: Magnesium is above iron in the reactivity series: it fizzes vigorously with dilute hydrochloric acid, whereas iron reacts slowly.
